analysis:
The only change in this file is a one-line edit near line 313 of EngineV2ProductionWiringTests.swift. The test helper's switch over MLXServerGenerationEvent now also skips a `.logprobs` case alongside `.toolCall` and `.toolCallDelta`. This looks like a test-only adaptation to a new enum case added elsewhere in the PR. No production code, wire protocol, key handling, attestation, cache storage or authorization logic changes in this file.

I examined the supplied base text at lines 1221-2591. That text is unchanged context, and it covers heartbeat grant tracking, request routing through the bridge, forced tool_choice validation, cacheScope/cacheSalt plumbing, logit_bias/seed overrides, cancellation propagation, KV-backend fallback on the heartbeat and prefill deadline configuration. Nothing in the test edit weakens those assertions. The skipped `.logprobs` case in the recorder does not affect the assertions that read the logprobs channel separately (lines 1850-1853).

The threat model touchpoint is T-041/TB-007. The tests assert that cacheSalt carries the tenant scope into the engine (line 1846), and that assertion is unaffected.

The source change that introduces `.logprobs` is outside this batch. A later pass should check that no production switch silently drops or leaks logprobs data, for example by sending it unencrypted or exposing it beyond the sealed response path (T-008). That is an integration question, not a finding here.
